confidence_notes: Restaurant and beer anchors rest on several undated or crowd-sourced UK sources, mainly a Scottish pub-price survey, a Holidu city comparison and budget-deal roundups, so they are approximate. Cocktail and wine anchors are weaker: they use Glasgow and Edinburgh crowd-sourced cocktail samples and a beer-to-wine relationship, not Inverness-specific data. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for a July peak-season window and do not reflect any inspected live listings. The FX observation is stale: the latest RBA observation I could verify is 2026-03-20, not one from near the 2026-10-16 generation date, and I could not retrieve the live RBA F11 table. The GBP to USD conversion of about 1.33 per pound is an assumption from general knowledge, not from a search, so the USD values carry that extra uncertainty.
comparable_city_reasoning: Regional basis is the Scottish Highlands, anchored to Inverness pub-price survey figures (roughly GBP 3.20 to 4.10 per pint, cappuccino about GBP 3 to 3.90) with a modest uplift for July tourist demand. Cocktail pricing is benchmarked to Glasgow and Edinburgh samples (GBP 10 to 11) with a discount for Inverness. Wine is set by the beer-to-wine relationship from UK restaurant pricing. Accommodation uses general knowledge of comparable Scottish Highland towns and is not based on any search.
